lead: The terminal is just another window. With six commands you can walk through your folders; with an AGENTS.md the agent knows who you are and what it may do; with Git you can undo any mistake.
objetivo: set up the agent's work folder with rules, a safety net, and secrets kept out of the text.

aprende.t: Walk through folders in the terminal
Keep keys out of the text

secoes.sub: You give the task, the agent works inside the folder, and you check.

nos.detalhe: You are still the one who decides: you ask, check the result, and accept or undo. Giving the task, checking, and deciding is management.
This is how you get to the folder and call the agent. On Windows, use cmd; on Mac and Linux, use Terminal.
Everything the agent needs to know lives here: the rules in AGENTS.md, the work in the files, the keys in .env (which Git ignores), and the history in .git.
The agent reads AGENTS.md before it starts, works on the files in the folder, and, if the rule asks for it, says what changed and how you can check.

secoes.volta: Don't like it? git restore brings the file back to the last saved version
secoes.legenda: The same files work for Claude Code and for Codex: both read AGENTS.md.

rolagem_fim.texto: You ask, the agent works inside the folder following AGENTS.md, and says what changed. You check. Like it? Commit. Don't like it? git restore.

secoes.titulo: The work cycle with the agent

texto: Inside the folder, run claude or codex and ask for just one thing, with the result you expect.
Start by asking it to read AGENTS.md: that way it follows your rules.

exemplo.texto: Read AGENTS.md. Create an index.html with a simple page about me, using what's in there.

texto: The agent creates and edits files in the folder. It may ask for permission before running commands.
Your role here is to read what it proposes, not to type for it.

exemplo.texto: The agent creates index.html and explains what it did.

texto: Open the result (the page in the browser, the summary, the file) and compare it with what you asked for.
Ask for at least one correction: it's the habit that separates using from managing.

exemplo.texto: Change the title to "HR Consulting" and add a contact section.

texto: Like it? git add . and git commit -m "..." save the version.
Don't like it? git restore index.html goes back to what was saved, no panic.

exemplo.texto: Make a commit before asking for a big change.

secoes.titulo: The files and commands in the sequence
secoes.sub: Copy and use. Replace the text between the < > signs with your own.

blocos.conteudo:
mkdir projetos
cd projetos
mkdir meu-primeiro-agente
cd meu-primeiro-agente
dir      # Windows (on Mac and Linux: ls)

# Who I am
<your name, your profession, who you work for>

# Rules for this project
- Write in English, short sentences.
- Don't delete files without asking.
- Before finishing, tell me what changed and how I can check it.
- Never write keys or passwords in a text file; they stay in the .env.

# What's in here
- index.html: my page

blocos.rot: Terminal · Git and keeping secrets out of the text
blocos.conteudo:
git init
echo .env> .gitignore
git add .
git commit -m "primeira versão"

# undo a change made by the agent:
git restore index.html

# the .env must NOT show up here:
git status

abas.html:
1. You get to the folder using only the terminal and can say which folder you're in.
  2. AGENTS.md has at least three rules written by you.
  3. The page opens in the browser and you asked for at least one correction.
  4. git status doesn't show the .env.

• Skipping Git: the agent's first bad change turns into manual rework.
  • Key in AGENTS.md: anything in plain text can end up on GitHub. Keys go only in the .env.
  • Vague request: "improve the page" produces a change you can't check. Ask for a result you can see.

secoes.sub: Do them in order. Only move on to the next one when the "done when" is true.

exercicios.titulo: E1 · First folder through the terminal
exercicios.texto: Create projetos/meu-primeiro-agente, go into it and list the contents. Open the same folder in Explorer (or Finder) and compare.
exercicios.pronto: you get to the folder using only the terminal, without the mouse, and can say which folder you're in.

exercicios.texto: Create AGENTS.md with who you are, the project rules, and what's in the folder.
exercicios.pronto: the file exists and has at least three rules of your own, written by you.

exercicios.texto: Call the agent and ask it to build the index.html from the AGENTS.md. Open it in the browser and ask for a change.
exercicios.pronto: the page opens and you asked the agent for at least one fix.

exercicios.texto: git init, add and commit. Ask for a big change and, if you don't like it, go back with git restore.
exercicios.pronto: you undid a change from the agent with one command, no panic.

exercicios.titulo: E5 · Secrets stay out of the text
exercicios.texto: Create a .env with a fake key and a .gitignore with the line .env. Add the rule to the AGENTS.md.
exercicios.pronto: git status does not show the .env.

exercicios.titulo: E6 · The agent reads your files
exercicios.texto: Put three of your texts in the folder and ask for a resumo.md with 5 decisions and 5 open items, citing the source of each one.
exercicios.pronto: you found at least two of the quoted sentences in the original.

secoes.sub: Six commands, one AGENTS.md and the first task.
The explanation appears after your answer.

perguntas.p: Where does an API key go in the project?
opcoes: In the AGENTS.md, so the agent knows how to use it.
In the index.html, as a comment.
In the .env, which is listed in the .gitignore.
perguntas.explica: Key only in the .env, and the .env in the .gitignore. That way git status does not show the file and it does not go to GitHub.

perguntas.p: The agent made a big change you did not approve. What do you do?
opcoes: git restore on the file, going back to the last saved version.
Ask the agent to try to remember how it was.
Delete the folder and start over.
Copy the old file from a manual backup.
perguntas.explica: With a commit before the change, git restore brings the file back in one command. That is why the rule: commit before asking for a big change.

opcoes: It is required only in Codex.
It is the manual the agent reads before working: who you are, the rules, and what is in the folder.
perguntas.explica: The AGENTS.md is the employee handbook. Claude Code and Codex read the same file, so the rules apply to both.
